## Agent Safety: Process Cleanup

This entire prompt — including this section — is passed to your runtime via
argv and is therefore visible in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` for your own process
and any sibling agents launched the same way. Pattern-based process matchers
read that file, so a command like `pkill -f <pattern>` will match its own
invoker whenever the pattern occurs anywhere in this prompt. Running such a
command can kill yourself, your parent shell, or peer agents mid-flight.

Hard bans — never issue these to clean up processes:
- `pkill -f <pattern>` (matches against full argv, including this prompt).
- `pgrep -f <pattern> | xargs kill` (same self-match hazard plus PID reuse).
- `killall <name>` where `<name>` is a shared interpreter or shell such as
  `python`, `node`, `claude`, or `bash` (kills unrelated processes).

Preferred alternatives, in order:
1. If you spawned the process yourself, capture its PID at spawn time
   (e.g. `mycmd & echo $!`, or read `$!` after backgrounding) and later
   `kill <pid>` that exact PID — no pattern matching needed.
2. If you did not spawn it but know its short command name (`comm`, max 15
   chars), use `pkill -x <comm>` for an exact-name match — `-x` does not
   read argv, so the self-match hazard is gone.
3. If `-f` is genuinely unavoidable, first run `pgrep -af <pattern>` and
   inspect the list. Exclude `$$`, `$PPID`, and every ancestor PID up the
   process tree before passing survivors to `kill`. Never pipe `pgrep -f`
   directly into `kill` or `xargs`.

## Task Description
修复 se3 webui running-flow 实时聊天视图在两种场景下「无法持续/正确显示对话记录」的 bug(#193 遗留的另一半,显示发送错误的部分已修复,本次专修「消息不显示」)。包含两个一并修复的症状:

【症状 A — 普通 session:`按1确定` respond 之后实时视图停止追加】
respond(对交互的确认)调用成功后,后续所有对话(agent 自动产出的下一步输出、以及用户之后再发送的消息)都不再出现在实时视图;必须退出再重进 running-flow 视图(触发 `/api/history` 全量快照)才能恢复,且重进后保持正常。该 session 内 `按1确定` 通常只发生一次,故无法稳定确认是否每次发送都触发,但已确认 respond 后必现。需排查并修复 respond(以及对称的 interject)成功后、daemon 推来的 `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` 增量未能到达 `/ws/ui` UI 客户端的问题:重点核查 `server/ws.py` 中「`MSG_HISTORY_DATA` 命中并 resolve 一个 pending REST pull waiter 时抑制对 `/ws/ui` 广播」的逻辑(约 lines 1087-1100),与前端 `app.js` 在 respond 后是否并发触发 REST 拉取所形成的竞态,确保 respond/interject 之后的新记录既能服务 REST waiter、又能正常增量推送给已订阅 ws 的实时视图,无需重进视图即可持续追加。

【症状 B — `--worktree` / discovery session:首条 assistant 回复正文为空,且之后无新消息】
以当前这个 worktree discovery session 为例:聊天框只显示用户初始描述与 assistant 条目的时间戳(`2026/6/14 15:09:44`),assistant 正文完全为空(渲染不出首条回复内容),其后也不再追加任何后续对话。需排查 worktree 会话 history 的读取/解析/增量推送/cursor 推进全链路,定位首条 assistant 正文读不出、且后续不追加的根因:重点核查 sidecar history 文件(`*.jsonl.from-*`)在 `daemon/history.py` 的 `read_flow` / `_iter_history_jsonl` / `_logical_step_id` 及其 cursor 映射中的处理是否完整,以及 worktree 会话的 `project_root` 是否在 respond/interject 与 history 读取链路中被正确保留,确保 worktree/discovery 会话的实时视图能完整、正确地显示首条及后续全部对话正文。

【验收】
1. 普通 session 中 `按1确定`(respond)之后,无需退出重进视图即可持续看到后续全部对话(agent 自动产出 + 用户后续发送的消息)。
2. `--worktree` / discovery session 中,首条 assistant 回复正文正常显示(非空),且后续消息持续实时追加。
3. 修复后运行相关测试(前端实时渲染/合并、`server/ws.py`、`server/state.py`、`daemon/history.py` 覆盖的用例),不得引入回归。

## Task Type
discovery

## Design Document
{
  "overview": "分两条独立链路修复。链路 A(普通 session 实时流中断):把 `server/ws.py` 中「resolve 了 REST pull waiter 即抑制 `/ws/ui` 广播」的粗粒度逻辑,收窄为「仅抑制按需 cache-miss pull 的 `mode: full` 回包广播」;对 `mode: append` 的实时增量,即使它恰好也 resolve 了某个 waiter,也必须继续广播给已订阅 ws 的实时视图。发起 REST 拉取的客户端经由 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重不会重复渲染,其余已订阅客户端则能持续收到增量。链路 B(worktree/discovery 首条空 + 后续不追加):在 `daemon/history.py` 的 sidecar 读取链路(`read_flow`/`_iter_history_jsonl`/`_logical_step_id` + cursor 映射)与 `read_active_flows` final-flush、`_resolve_flow_dir` 的 `project_root` 解析上,确保 worktree 会话的 `project_root` 被完整保留并能定位到正确的 history 目录,首条 assistant 正文与后续记录均能被读出并增量推送。",
  "architecture_decisions": [
    {
      "decision": "症状 A 的根因修复落在服务端 `ws.py`/`state.py`,而非依赖前端绕过。",
      "rationale": "记录已正确到达服务端缓存(重进视图触发全量快照即恢复证明缓存完整),失败的只是 `/ws/ui` 增量广播这一跳;在广播抑制点按 `mode` 收窄是最小、最精确的修复面,且对所有订阅客户端一致生效。",
      "alternatives_considered": "在前端 respond 后主动轮询 `/api/history/{flow_id}` 拉增量——会放大 REST 压力且复活 waiter 竞态;或让前端在 respond 后强制全量重载——正是当前需要消除的「必须重进视图」体验。"
    },
    {
      "decision": "区分 `mode: full`(按需 pull 回包,抑制广播)与 `mode: append`(实时增量,始终广播),而非区分「是否 resolve 了 waiter」。",
      "rationale": "抑制广播的真正目的是避免把 cache-miss pull 的全量帧再广播出去导致全体客户端 progress token 被清空;该目的只针对 `mode: full`。`mode: append` 帧无论是否凑巧 resolve waiter,都承载实时增量,必须送达订阅者。",
      "alternatives_considered": "维持「resolve 即抑制」并改为只对发起者单播——`UiHub` 是按 owner 广播,无法精确单播到发起 REST 的那一个连接,且会漏掉同 owner 其他订阅客户端。"
    },
    {
      "decision": "症状 B 在 `daemon/history.py`/`client.py` 内修复 `project_root` 保留与 sidecar 首条解析,前端仅做兜底校验。",
      "rationale": "首条正文为空且 cursor 不前进是读取侧问题:final-flush 路径 `read_flow(flow_id, cursor=cursor)` 缺失 `project_root` 会导致 `_resolve_flow_dir` 在错误的 roots 集合中查找;worktree 会话的 root 解析需统一。源头修好后前端 `normalizeRecord` 无需特例。",
      "alternatives_considered": "仅在前端 normalize 层兜底空正文——治标不治本,后续记录仍因 cursor/root 解析失败而不追加。"
    },
    {
      "decision": "前端复用既有 `dedupeAppendRecords`/`reconcileLocalEchoes`/`mergeSnapshotWithLiveAppends`,不新增第二套去重路径。",
      "rationale": "running-flow-console 规范已要求 append 路径经 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重;服务端放行 append 后产生的「REST 响应 + ws 广播」重叠正落在该函数的设计职责内,只需补测试确认覆盖 respond/interject 后场景。",
      "alternatives_considered": "在 applyHistoryData 新增针对 respond 的特判去重——与现有去重职责重复,增加漂移风险。"
    }
  ],
  "components": [
    {
      "name": "server/ws.py — MSG_HISTORY_DATA 广播分支",
      "responsibilities": "在 resolve pull waiter 后,按 `mode` 决定是否广播:`mode == full` 且 resolve 了 pull 则抑制(REST 回包负责送达);其余(含所有 `mode == append` 实时增量)始终调用 `_push_history_data` 广播给该 owner 的 `/ws/ui` 客户端。",
      "interfaces": "`handle_daemon_message` 的 `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` 分支;`HistoryRequestRegistry.resolve(...) -> bool`;`_push_history_data(hub, state, machine_id, flow_id, mode, records)`。"
    },
    {
      "name": "server/state.py — append_history / get_history_snapshot",
      "responsibilities": "确认 `append` 在 bundle 存在时正确 extend 并返回 `applied=True`、保持 generation 稳定;确保被广播的 append 与 REST 全量回包对同一 bundle 快照一致,不产生 token/generation 漂移。",
      "interfaces": "`append_history(flow_id, mode, records, *, cursor, machine_id) -> bool`;`get_history_snapshot(...)`。"
    },
    {
      "name": "daemon/history.py — sidecar 读取与 cursor/root 解析",
      "responsibilities": "保证 `_iter_history_jsonl` 同时枚举 `*.jsonl` 与 `*.jsonl.from-*`;`_logical_step_id`/`parse_step_type_from_step_id` 正确归并;`read_flow` 首条记录正文被读出、cursor/`_read_offsets` 正确推进;`read_active_flows` final-flush 传入 `project_root`;`_resolve_flow_dir` 正确定位 worktree 会话目录。",
      "interfaces": "`read_flow(flow_id, *, project_root, cursor) -> FlowRead`;`read_active_flows(cursors)`;`_resolve_flow_dir(flow_id, project_root)`;`_iter_history_jsonl(flow_dir)`;`_logical_step_id(filename)`。"
    },
    {
      "name": "daemon/client.py — project_root 在 respond/interject 与 history push 链路保留",
      "responsibilities": "确保 respond/interject 处理与 `_push_history`/`read_active_flows` 调用链中,worktree 会话的 `project_root` 不丢失(尤其 final-flush 与 `_resolve_interject_root` 路径)。",
      "interfaces": "`_push_history(ws, force_index)`;`_resolve_interject_root(flow_id)`;`_respond_handler`/`_interject_handler` 调用约定。"
    },
    {
      "name": "static/app.js — applyHistoryData / 实时追加去重",
      "responsibilities": "确认 respond/interject 后,服务端放行的 append 帧经 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重后正确追加渲染,既不重复也不丢失;worktree 首条记录 normalize 后正文非空(若源头已修则仅校验)。",
      "interfaces": "`applyHistoryData(msg)`;`dedupeAppendRecords(existing, incoming)`;`normalizeRecord(...)`;`reconcileLocalEchoes(records)`。"
    }
  ],
  "data_flow": "症状 A:用户在实时视图 `respond`/`interject` → `POST /api/flows/{id}/respond|interject` → daemon 写 `.response`/interjection 文件并消费 → 运行循环产出新记录 → daemon `_push_history` 经 `read_active_flows` 增量读出 → `make_history_data(mode=append)` 发往 server → `ws.py` `append_history`(applied=True)→【修复点】按 `mode` 判断:append 始终 `_push_history_data` 广播 → `/ws/ui` → 前端 `applyHistoryData` 经 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重后增量渲染,持续追加。症状 B:worktree/discovery 会话运行 → 记录写入会话 history 目录(含运行态及 merge-back sidecar `*.jsonl.from-*`)→ daemon `read_active_flows` 用 `meta.project_root` 调 `read_flow`(及 final-flush 路径,需带 `project_root`)→ `_resolve_flow_dir` 定位正确目录 → `_iter_history_jsonl` 枚举主文件+sidecar,`_logical_step_id` 归并,逐行读出首条 assistant 正文与后续记录、推进 cursor/`_read_offsets` → `make_history_data` → server 缓存并广播 → 前端 normalize 后完整渲染首条及后续。",
  "testing_strategy": "Python(pytest):1) 扩充 `tests/test_server_history.py` 并新增 `tests/test_server_history_live_append_broadcast.py`,断言:resolve 了 pull 的 `mode: full` 帧不广播;`mode: append` 帧即使 resolve 了 waiter 也广播;respond/interject 后连续 append 持续广播到 `/ws/ui`(用 fake hub 计数广播)。2) 扩充 `tests/test_worktree_history_sidecar.py`/`tests/test_daemon_history.py`,断言:worktree 会话首条 assistant 正文非空、后续记录随 cursor 推进被增量读出;final-flush 路径带 `project_root` 能定位目录;主文件与 sidecar 归并到同一逻辑步且无丢失/重复。前端(node mjs):新增 `tests/frontend/live_append_after_respond.test.mjs` 并扩充 `tests/frontend/test_app_pure.mjs`,断言:respond 后 append 帧经 `dedupeAppendRecords` 去重后持续追加、不重复、不丢失,且不误伤 `partial`/`stream_progress` 累积分片。最后运行规范覆盖的相关测试集(`server/ws.py`、`server/state.py`、`daemon/history.py`、前端实时渲染/合并)并对照 `preexisting_test_failures.md` 排除既有失败,确保无新增回归。"
}

# SE3 Framework — Base Specification

## Purpose
Project baseline conventions. This spec is generated by `se3 init` and is automatically loaded in every `se3 run` flow.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Project Identity
- Project name: SE3 Framework
- Summary: the SE 3.0 code-first software-engineering flow engine — a pure CLI flow engine; code is primary, and the spec is a documented snapshot of the code's current state (a spec-assistant), refreshed from the code by `se3 sync`
- Primary language/framework: Python 3.8+, Typer (CLI), PyYAML, Rich, prompt-toolkit

### Requirement: Directory Structure
- `src/se3/` — framework source code (a pip-installable package)
  - `cli.py` — CLI entry point; registers all commands
  - `commands/` — implementations of the individual CLI subcommands
  - `engine/` — flow engine core (state machine, steps, context builder, LLM caller)
    - `engine/sync_engine.py` — the `se3 sync` single-round stateless engine (spec ↔ code drift analysis and write-back); `run_once` accepts each round's analyze_specs subset and the do_discovery flag, aggregates the files touched by each spec's analyze this round into cumulative deps, and exposes the count of newly discovered subsystems this round along with the obsolete-spec candidates
    - `engine/sync_loop.py` — the `se3 sync` cross-round orchestration (convergence detection, oscillation guard, consecutive infrastructure-failure counting, checkpoint writing, and `--resume` continuation); before the round loop it applies a level-1 global shutter and level-2 per-spec gate skip based on sync_state, within the round loop it performs a level-3 per-spec early exit (tracking each spec's consecutive zero-drift round count), and after convergence it deletes obsolete specs and writes sync_state
    - `engine/sync_analyzer.py` — spec/code comparison and LLM response parsing for the sync phase; strips the markdown fence before `json.loads`; on JSON parse failure it records `failed_analysis_reason` instead of synthesizing a fake CONFLICT diff; consumes the touched-files exposed by llm_caller for this call to support per-spec dependency tracking
    - `engine/sync_discovery.py` — within sync, discovers missing specs via the LLM and generates new specs (can be invoked every round and runs to its own convergence); a newly created spec must pass `spec_validator.validate_spec_structure(...)` before being written to disk; also provides the obsolete-spec deletion entry point `delete_obsolete_specs` (after convergence, deletes the `se3/specs/<name>/` directory; deletes directly by default, with optional per-item human confirmation)
    - `engine/sync_interaction.py` — interactive prompts for the sync flow (high-risk deletion approval, quota-exhaustion pause, etc.)
    - `engine/sync_checkpoint.py` — a lightweight persistence module for sync continuation (a schema v1 dataclass, atomic write to `se3/state/sync_checkpoint.json`, recomputing in-sync specs by SHA-256)
    - `engine/sync_state.py` — the persistent incremental-optimization cache module for sync: the `SyncState` dataclass (`state_version` / `converged_at` / `code_fingerprint` / `discovery_converged` / `spec_deps` / `obsolete_specs`), atomic write to `se3/state/sync_state.json`; JSON corruption / version mismatch / missing file all return no cache; provides `compute_code_fingerprint` (an overall hash of sorted git ls-files blob shas + the content hash of untracked, non-ignored files, excluding `se3/`), file content hashing, and file add/delete/rename detection; records the "last successful convergence" snapshot, completely different in semantics and lifecycle from `sync_checkpoint.py` (the interrupt-recovery transient state)
    - `engine/spec_validator.py` — a pure-functional spec structure validator that enforces the spec-format v1 contract (the v1 marker, the `# <name> Specification` title, `## Purpose`, at least one `### Requirement:`, a non-narrative first line); reused in three places: sync_discovery, sync_engine, and `se3 sync --validate-only`
    - `engine/state_machine.py` — the finite-state-machine core of the `se3 run` flow engine, driving transitions between steps and the flow of context
    - `engine/steps/` — the implementation package for the individual `se3 run` steps (analyze / plan / implement / verify, etc.)
    - `engine/context_builder.py` — builds context for the LLM subprocess (injecting the spec, history summary, current task, etc.)
    - `engine/llm_caller.py` — the unified entry point for LLM calls, responsible for iterating/rotating through the agent command list, detecting quota exhaustion and timeouts, and wrapping call results
    - `engine/chat_history.py` — multi-turn conversation history management and persistence
    - `engine/dag_scheduler.py` — a DAG-based task scheduler that resolves dependencies between steps/tasks and executes them in topological order
    - `engine/issue_discovery.py` — the issue discovery flow implementation; scans code/spec and produces pending issues
    - `engine/issue_manager.py` — reading/writing, status management, and deduplication of the issue records under `se3/issues/`
    - `engine/docs_updater.py` — documentation auto-update logic (e.g., syncing README, spec summaries, etc.)
    - `engine/version_bumper.py` — computes and bumps the version number based on the commit type (bugfix/feature) and the previous version baseline
    - `engine/version_script_interface.py` — the version-script interface adapter layer; provides discovery of the project's version-management script (probing candidate paths such as `scripts/version.py`), on-demand generation (written to disk from `templates/version_script.py.tmpl`), and a unified invocation entry point (subprocess wrappers for the `get` / `bump` / `set` subcommands), so that `engine/version_bumper.py` can read and bump the version without coupling directly to a specific script path
    - `engine/worktree.py` — the engine-side wrapper for git worktree operations, used together with the `se3/worktrees/` directory
    - `engine/merge/` — implementation related to the multi-worktree / multi-branch merge flow (see the engine-internals spec's "Engine Merge Submodules" Requirement for the specific submodules)
  - `templates/` — project-initialization templates (base spec, README, version-management script, version history, etc.)
    - `base_spec.md` — the initial template for a new project's base spec; written by `se3 init` to `se3/specs/base/spec.md`
    - `readme_md.md` — the new-project README template, containing formattable placeholders such as `{project_name}` / `{project_description}` / `{project_overview}`
    - `versions_md.md` — the new-project version-history document template (`VERSIONS.md`), containing the `{project_name}` / `{date}` placeholders
    - `version_script.py.tmpl` — the project version-management script template, providing a unified interface for the three subcommands `get` / `bump` / `set`; the output contract is: on success, print the version string to stdout and exit 0; on failure, print the error to stderr and exit 1
  - `agent_runner.py` — the Agent runner abstract base class (the `AgentRunner` ABC, `RunResult`, the `InfraErrorType` enum); defines a unified agent execution interface to ease future extension to multiple runner types (API-based, other CLIs, etc.)
  - `claude_runner.py` — the Claude Code CLI single-command adapter (`ClaudeCodeRunner`); implements the `AgentRunner` interface and is responsible for invoking the Claude Code CLI via a subprocess; agent selection/rotation is handled by `LLMCaller`; the `ClaudeRunner` alias is retained for backward compatibility
  - `codex_runner.py` — the OpenAI Codex CLI single-command adapter (`CodexRunner`); implements the `AgentRunner` interface and wraps a single `codex exec --json` invocation, normalizing Codex's JSONL event stream into Claude-compatible stream-json NDJSON so all upstream consumers stay runner-agnostic; constructed for `type: codex` agents by `LLMCaller._create_runner`
  - `config.py` — SE3 configuration management (`se3.yaml`, `se3.local.yaml` loading, git worktree main-repository root resolution, Claude subprocess config loading)
  - `utils.py` — shared utility functions (such as `discover_specs`, specs-directory resolution, etc.; supports `se3/specs/` first, `specs/` fallback, and the legacy `openspec/specs/` path)
  - `core/` — the core-utilities subpackage
    - `utils.py` — core utility functions shared across the framework (such as the `truncate_preview` formatting helper)
  - `daemon/` — the resident control-plane daemon package (the implementation of the `se3 daemon` subcommand); ships in the same package and wheel as the core and evolves in version lockstep; responsible for discovering/supervising local `se3 run` flows, spawning new flows on their behalf, aggregating `se3/state|logs|calls|issues` state, and maintaining one outbound connection to the central server (see the daemon spec's "Daemon Modules" Requirement for the specific submodules)
  - `server/` — the central-server backend plus bundled web frontend package; not a subcommand of the core `se3`, launched through the separate console_scripts entry point `se3-server`; the heavy web dependencies (FastAPI/uvicorn/websockets) are isolated via `pyproject.toml` optional-dependencies (`se3[server]`), so the core CLI is unaffected when they are not installed (see the server spec's "Server Modules" Requirement for the specific submodules)
- `se3/` — the SE3 runtime directory (gitignored, except specs/)
  - `specs/` — project specifications (committed to git)
  - `state/` — flow engine state (gitignored), holding various runtime-persisted artifacts:
    - `state/sync_checkpoint.json` — the continuation checkpoint written when `se3 sync` is interrupted (cleared on normal convergence / successful `--resume` completion)
    - `state/sync_state.json` — the persistent incremental cache for `se3 sync` (the "last successful convergence" snapshot), recording the global content fingerprint, whether discovery has converged, each spec's spec_hash and dependency file set, and the obsolete-spec candidate set; written only when sync truly converges with no unresolved failed analyses; unlike `sync_checkpoint.json` — the latter is an interrupt-recovery transient state cleared on convergence, while the former is a build cache that persists across invocations; ignored by the `/se3/*` `.gitignore` rule (a required property: being tracked by git would carry a stale cache across machines and cause a false in-sync determination)
    - `state/engine.json` — the persisted state of the `se3 run` state machine (current step, context, iteration count, etc.), used to support `--resume` continuation after a flow is interrupted
    - `state/test_baseline_cache.json` — the pre-implement test-baseline cache (atomic write, corruption-tolerant), keyed by git HEAD sha + working-tree dirty hash, recording the set of failing test IDs measured at flow start so parallel/resumed flows on the same commit reuse it; used by the flow engine to distinguish newly introduced regressions from inherited (pre-existing) failures (replaces the retired auto-accumulated `state/known_test_failures.json` known-list — see flow-engine *Pre-implement Test Baseline*)
    - `state/baseline_fix_attempts.json` — mechanism B's cross-flow persistent memory (atomic write, corruption-tolerant, schema-versioned, LRU-bounded) of inherited (baseline) test failures the bounded fix loop has *given up* on, keyed per `test_id` with an accumulated attempt count and the latest reason; read so later flows never re-loop a fundamentally un-fixable baseline failure; managed by `engine/baseline_fix_memory.py` and ignored by the `/se3/*` `.gitignore` rule (see flow-engine *Test Step Configuration and Multi-Phase Execution*)
    - `state/merge.lock` — the project's main-worktree mutex lock file (based on `fcntl.flock` + PID stale detection), acquired with **blocking** (queue-and-wait) semantics; held by a synchronous `se3 run` for the duration of its run and by every `se3 merge`, so synchronous runs and merges serialize against each other (worktree-mode flow bodies run lock-free and contend only at their final merge)
    - `state/summary-*.md` / `state/summary-*.json` — summary snapshots produced at each flow phase (markdown for humans to read, JSON for downstream programs to consume)
    - `state/archive/` — the archive subdirectory for completed or superseded old state files, used for investigating historical flows
  - `cache/` — the cache index
  - `logs/` — execution logs
  - `calls/` — the human-call queue
  - `collab/` — multi-agent collaboration state (retired: the collab capability was removed; the runtime directory is no longer produced or consumed, and the merge runtime-sync tier no longer references `collab/tasks/`. Issue `#002 Autonomous Collaboration` remains open as the intent to rebuild this capability in the future)
  - `history/` — the historical session/flow archive (gitignored), retaining archived artifacts of past `se3 run` / `se3 sync` flows
  - `issues/` — the issue records produced by the issue discovery flow (gitignored), read/written by the issue-discovery-related commands
  - `tmp/` — the temporary-file directory (gitignored), used for flow intermediate artifacts (such as the LLM subprocess's prompt / response snapshots)
  - `worktrees/` — the git worktree workspace directory (gitignored), created and maintained by the worktree-management-related flows to isolate parallel tasks
- `.claude/` — the framework specifications that development depends on (read-only, must not be modified)
- `tests/` — pytest tests
- `scripts/` — helper scripts

### Requirement: Coding Conventions
- Python style follows standard PEP 8
- CLI commands are registered with Typer; complex commands use a sub-typer (`add_typer`), while simple commands with positional arguments use `@app.command`
- Logging uses the `logging` module, with each module declaring `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`
- Type annotations use the `from __future__ import annotations` style
- Test files are placed in the `tests/` directory, named `test_*.py`, and use pytest

### Requirement: Key Constraints
- **Bootstrapping constraint**: this project is a bootstrapping project — it both generates new specifications and develops using the published specifications. When generating new specifications, the published specifications under `.claude/` must not be changed
- **Spec read-only**: specs under `se3/specs/` should not be modified arbitrarily during implementation; modifications must pass the spec guardrails check
- **LLM subprocess**: some steps of the flow engine (such as analyze, plan) are executed via an LLM subprocess; these subprocesses cannot access CLAUDE.md and can only obtain project conventions through the spec

### Requirement: Workflow Conventions
- Use `se3 commit` instead of `git commit` (enforces passing tests, intercepts sensitive files)
- Commit messages must include context so the next session can resume easily
- A feature may only be marked complete after tests have been run
- Main entry command: `se3 run "task description"`

### Requirement: CLI Command Modules
Each module under `src/se3/commands/` corresponds to one or a group of `se3` subcommands, registered to the Typer app by `src/se3/cli.py`. New commands must be registered in this spec to prevent the LLM subprocess from being unable to discover command boundaries when CLAUDE.md is absent.

- `run.py` — `se3 run`, the unified entry point for the SE3 3.0 flow engine; replaces the old start/work/done trio of commands and is driven by the state machine; supports creating a new flow, `--resume` continuation, `--worktree` isolation mode (runs the flow in an isolated git worktree and auto-merges back via the heavy `se3 merge` orchestrator on success), and `--type=<bugfix|feature>` task-type annotation
- `sync.py` — `se3 sync`, drives `SyncLoop` to perform one-directional code → spec synchronization until convergence; supports switches such as `--once`, `--max-rounds`, `--stable-rounds`, `--interactive`, `--show-diff`, `--resume`, and `--validate-only`; writes only specs, never modifies code; also provides the `process_call_response` entry point for `se3 sync-respond` to handle the human response file for high-risk deletion approvals
- `cli.py::sync_respond_cmd` — `se3 sync-respond <call-file-path>`, handles the human response call file written out by the `se3 sync` flow in scenarios such as the interactive high-impact deletion approval (high-impact deletion call); delegates to `commands/sync.py::process_call_response` to parse the response and advance the sync flow
- `init_cmd.py` — `se3 init`, initializes a new SE3 project; lays down templates such as `se3.yaml`, the base spec, README, `VERSIONS.md`, and the version-management script (registered by `cli.py` via the `@app.command(name="init")` decorator)
- `history_cmd.py` — `se3 history`, viewing and managing session/flow history; subcommands include `list`, `show <flow_id>`, `restore <flow_id>`, and `archived`
- `issue_cmd.py` — `se3 issue`, reading/writing the issue records produced by issue discovery; subcommands include `list` (open-only by default, supports `--all`), `show <id>`, `create` (interactive), and `reset <id>` (resets in-progress back to open)
- `merge_cmd.py` — `se3 merge <branch> [...]`, merges branches sequentially into the current branch; supports `--strategy=default|strict|fast` and `--delete-merged`
- `merge_respond.py` — `se3 merge-respond <call-file-path>`, handles the human/external response files written out via the MCP call queue during the merge flow
- `salvage_cmd.py` — `se3 salvage`, best-effort salvage of work from an abnormally terminated session; fault-tolerantly reads session state, evaluates the git diff, commits existing changes, creates issues for unfinished work, and archives the session, with each step independently fault-tolerant
- `cli.py::guardrails_cmd` — `se3 guardrails`, runs the SE3 Spec Guardrails checks (the spec-format v1 contract, structural constraints, etc.) against the spec files under `se3/specs/`, used to intercept non-compliant spec changes at the commit / sync / CI stages; this command is registered directly in `src/se3/cli.py` via `@app.command(name="guardrails")`, with no separate `commands/guardrails_cmd.py` module file
- `cli.py::daemon_app` — `se3 daemon`, the management subcommand group for the resident control-plane daemon (`start` / `stop` / `status`), registered to `cli.py`'s sub-typer via `add_typer`. `start` launches the daemon as a detached background process by default (`--foreground` keeps it attached to the terminal, `--server-url` specifies the central server address); `stop` stops the running daemon; `status` reports the daemon's running state and tracked flows (`--json` outputs JSON). This command group is defined directly in `src/se3/cli.py`, while the daemon implementation lives in the `src/se3/daemon/` package; imports of the `daemon` package are always deferred into the command body so that core CLI startup is unaffected
- `merge/` — the subpackage of merge-related supporting modules, used by `merge_cmd.py` and `engine/merge/`:
  - `failure_reason.py` — the `FailureReason` IntEnum, replacing the ~60 failure_reason string literals scattered across the old orchestrator, to ease typed dispatch downstream
  - `result_model.py` — the typed result model for the merge orchestrator, split by per-branch outcome (success / failure / skipped), distinguishing `newly_merged` / `already_merged_branches` / `with_warnings`
  - `postcondition.py` — postcondition assertions for the merge success path (three independent conditions: ancestry, merge commit, version bumped)
  - `merge_lock.py` — the project's main-worktree mutex (`MergeLock`) based on `fcntl.flock` + PID-based stale detection; supports a **blocking** acquire (`LOCK_EX`, queue-and-wait) used by `se3 merge` and by synchronous `se3 run` (which holds it for the whole run), as well as the legacy non-blocking (`LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB`) fail-fast acquire retained as a fallback
  - `llm_trace.py` — an append-only JSONL trace log of every LLM call during `se3 merge`; each record is `flush`ed after writing (immediately visible via the page cache), but `os.fsync` is changed to batched / reduced-frequency (forced every N records or T seconds by default, and forced on `stop()` / file rotation / process exit) to mitigate the dirty-page write-back IO amplification caused by multiple parallel merge groups streaming trace writes combined with the daemon stat-ing all files every tick; output to `se3/logs/llm/merge_<timestamp>_<seq>.jsonl`
  - `secret_redact.py` — redacts common secret patterns (`sk-...`, `ak-...`, `Bearer <token>`, `ghp_...`, `pypi-...`, `npm_...`, TOML/JSON/YAML password fields, etc.) before writing to the merge log/trace

### Requirement: Agent Runner Abstraction
- Agent execution is unified through the `AgentRunner` abstract base class interface (`src/se3/agent_runner.py`); every concrete runner must implement this interface
- The `InfraErrorType` enum defines the infrastructure error types that require agent rotation: `NONE`, `USAGE_LIMIT`, `TIMEOUT`, `HANG`, `STARTUP_FAILURE`
- The `RunResult` dataclass represents a runner's execution result, used by the upper-layer flow engine to judge success/failure and rotation decisions
- There are two concrete implementations: `ClaudeCodeRunner` (`src/se3/claude_runner.py`), wrapping a single Claude Code CLI command invocation, and `CodexRunner` (`src/se3/codex_runner.py`), wrapping a single OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`) invocation and normalizing Codex's JSONL events into Claude-compatible stream-json NDJSON. `LLMCaller._create_runner` dispatches on the agent's `type` (`claude-code` / `codex`); the logic for iterating/rotating the agent command list lives in `LLMCaller`. The `AgentRunner` ABC contract is `run` / `run_with_monitor` / `detect_infra_error` / `build_call_args`, the last of which lets `LLMCaller` pass call intent (effective prompt, read-only flag, context files) and have each runner translate it into its own CLI flags
- On the Linux platform, `psutil` is used for subprocess resource monitoring to detect abnormal states such as hangs
- This abstraction allows new runner types (API-based, other CLI tools, etc.) to be added in the future without changing the upper-layer callers

### Requirement: Configuration Management
- Project configuration is loaded uniformly through `src/se3/config.py`, supporting two configuration files:
  - `se3.yaml` — the main configuration (committed to git)
  - `se3.local.yaml` — the local override configuration (gitignored)
- Configuration loading supports git worktree detection: by comparing `--git-common-dir` with `--git-dir`, it automatically resolves from a worktree back to the main repository's working-tree root to read the main repository's configuration
- The Claude subprocess configuration is loaded via `load_claude_subprocess_config`, and the Claude command list via `load_claude_commands`, for use by `ClaudeCodeRunner` / `LLMCaller`

### Requirement: Shared Utilities
- `src/se3/utils.py` provides shared utility functions across commands, including spec discovery (`discover_specs`), etc.
- Specs-directory resolution order: `se3/specs/` first → `specs/` fallback → the legacy `openspec/specs/` path, to ease migration from older versions
- The `src/se3/core/` subpackage holds lower-level core utilities, decoupled from the project's business logic:
  - `truncate_preview(text, max_length, ellipsis_str)` — consistent preview truncation and ellipsis formatting, used for console output

### Requirement: utils.py Helper Functions
Besides the spec-discovery entry points (`discover_specs` / `_resolve_specs_dir`), `src/se3/utils.py` also centrally maintains a set of helper functions reused by CLI commands, the flow engine, and documentation/status tools. New functions here must be registered in this spec to help sub-agents discover reusable tools when CLAUDE.md is absent.

- **Spec parsing and change discovery**
  - `parse_spec(filepath)` — parses a single spec.md file, returning a dict with keys such as `title` (the `#` header), `purpose` (the `## Purpose` content), `requirements` (the `### Requirement:` list, each with `title` / `level` / `content` / `scenarios` / `line`), and `scenarios` (each with `title` / `when` / `then` / `line`)
  - `discover_changes(path="se3/specs/_changelog")` — discovers the list of change names under the changelog directory, consumed by the change-management flow
  - `discover_specs_in_change(change_name, base_path="openspec/changes")` — lists the specs involved within a given change directory
- **Execution results and artifacts**
  - `get_exit_code(results)` — aggregates a unified exit code from a set of result records, used to wrap up CLI commands
  - `discover_outputs(path)` — enumerates the list of artifact files under the given path
  - `get_file_mtime(path)` — safely reads a file's mtime, returning `None` when the file does not exist
  - `copy_file(src, dst)` — copies a file, automatically creating the destination parent directory first if it does not exist
- **Project structure and documentation consistency**
  - `get_source_mappings(project_root)` — returns the mapping between the project's source code and its specs / documentation
  - `find_verification_markers(scenario_id, search_paths)` — finds the verification markers corresponding to a specific scenario within the given set of paths
  - `get_framework_version(project_root)` — reads and returns the SE3 framework version string referenced by the project
  - `check_documentation_consistency(...)` — performs a consistency check across documents such as README / spec / status
  - `has_framework_file_changes(project_root)` — returns `(bool, List[str])`, indicating whether there are framework-file changes in the current working tree and the specific list of paths
  - `parse_status_md(filepath="./status.md")` — parses the project's `status.md` status file and returns a structured dict

### Requirement: Project Init Templates
- `src/se3/templates/` holds all the template files needed to initialize a new project, used by `se3 init`-type commands when scaffolding a new project
- Templates fall into two categories:
  - directly copied markdown templates (`base_spec.md`, `readme_md.md`, `versions_md.md`) — typically containing placeholder fields such as `{project_name}`, `{project_description}`, `{project_overview}`, `{date}`, which require string-format substitution before use
  - an executable script template (`version_script.py.tmpl`) — once written to disk, it serves as a standalone runnable Python script within the target project
- `version_script.py.tmpl` defines the unified interface contract for an SE3 project's version-management script:
  - It must support three subcommands: `get` (read the current version), `bump --type {major|minor|patch}` (bump the version by type), and `set --version X.Y.Z` (set the version directly)
  - Output contract: on success, print the version string to stdout and exit with exit code 0; on failure, print the error message to stderr and exit with exit code 1
  - This contract is depended upon by flow modules such as `engine/version_bumper.py`, so the template's output format and exit codes must not be changed without updating the callers
- When adding a file under `templates/`, it must be registered in both this spec and `src/se3/templates/__init__.py` so upper-layer commands can discover and use it
- The current implementation of `src/se3/templates/__init__.py` contains only a single package-level docstring (`"""SE3 templates for project initialization."""`), existing as a Python package marker; it does not yet enumerate the concrete template-file list there via `__all__` / constants / a dict / etc. When adding a template, the registration action must at minimum occur in this spec file; the synchronized registration mechanism in `__init__.py` may be implemented later as actual need arises, but must not conversely weaken the "must be registered" constraint

### Requirement: Engine Co-located Test Modules
As a controlled exception to the Coding Conventions general rule that "test files go in the `tests/` directory", `src/se3/engine/` is permitted to contain pytest test modules co-located with the engine source code, used to cover tightly coupled internal engine behavior (private helper functions, internal state-machine branches, step-internal details, etc.). New such co-located test modules must be registered in this spec to prevent the LLM subprocess from misjudging them as violating files that should be moved to `tests/` when CLAUDE.md is absent.

- `src/se3/engine/test_e2e.py` — flow-engine end-to-end tests, covering the cross-step integration paths of the `se3 run` state machine
- `src/se3/engine/test_engine.py` — unit/integration tests for the engine core (state machine / context / persistence, etc.)
- `src/se3/engine/test_steps.py` — the collection of tests for the step implementations under `engine/steps/`
- `src/se3/engine/test_version_bumper.py` — tests for the version-bump logic of `engine/version_bumper.py`

### Requirement: Runtime Dependencies
- The project's runtime dependencies are declared in `[project].dependencies` of `pyproject.toml`, including:
  - `typer>=0.9.0` — the CLI framework
  - `pyyaml>=6.0` — YAML configuration parsing (`se3.yaml`, `se3.local.yaml`, etc.)
  - `rich>=13.0.0` — terminal rich-text rendering (logs, tables, status display, etc.)
  - `prompt-toolkit>=3.0.0` — interactive command-line input support (for scenarios requiring terminal input such as interactive prompts and the human-call queue)
  - `psutil>=5.9.0` — cross-platform process probing (hang detection in `claude_runner.py`, local `se3 run` process discovery in `daemon/supervisor.py`); a core runtime dependency
- The central server's heavy web dependencies are isolated via `[project.optional-dependencies]` in `pyproject.toml`, introduced only when the `se3[server]` extra is installed, so they do not pollute the core CLI installation:
  - `fastapi` — the web framework for the central-server backend
  - `uvicorn` — the ASGI server, launched by the `se3-server` entry point
  - `websockets` — WebSocket protocol support for daemon↔server and the frontend
  - `argon2-cffi>=21.3.0` — slow password hashing (argon2id) for the built-in multi-tenant local auth provider; the crypto layer (`server/crypto.py`) prefers argon2-cffi and falls back to `bcrypt` only when argon2 is unavailable. It is kept in the `[server]` extra so a core-only install never imports it — `se3.cli` / `se3.daemon` must not depend on argon2.
- The central server's persistence layer (`server/persistence.py`) uses the standard-library `sqlite3` module for its embedded single-file store, so it adds NO new third-party dependency — the embedded-sqlite choice matches the zero-external-dependency, single-file deployment goal.
- When only `se3` (without `[server]`) is installed, the core `se3` command family must not raise import errors due to server code; references to the `se3.server` package and its heavy dependencies must be deferred until the `se3-server` entry point actually runs
- When adding a runtime dependency, `pyproject.toml` must be updated in sync and it must be registered in this spec, so subprocesses / sub-agents know what libraries are available

# daemon Specification

## Purpose

The resident control-plane daemon package (`se3 daemon`): discovers/supervises local `se3 run` flows, aggregates `se3/state|logs|calls|issues` state, and maintains one outbound connection to the central server.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Daemon Modules

`src/se3/daemon/` is the implementation package for the resident control-plane daemon, driven by the `se3 daemon` subcommand (registered in `cli.py`). The daemon outlives `se3 run` and is the only component that can keep aggregating state and exposing a stable endpoint after the CLI exits. New daemon submodules must be registered in this spec to prevent the LLM subprocess from being unable to discover module boundaries when CLAUDE.md is absent.

- `daemon.py` — the daemon process entry point and lifecycle: `DaemonConfig` (a config dataclass containing `pid_dir`, defaulting to `~/.se3`, overridable via `SE3_DAEMON_DIR`, and storing `daemon.pid` / `daemon_status.json` / `daemon.log` side by side, plus the optional secret `daemon_key` field — the credential the daemon presents in HELLO so the multi-tenant server can resolve it to an owner; it is sourced from `se3 daemon start --daemon-key` or the `SE3_DAEMON_KEY` environment variable, propagated to spawned `se3 run` subprocesses via the `SE3_DAEMON_KEY` child-env var, and never written to the status file or log), `Daemon` (the asyncio event loop), the `start_daemon` / `stop_daemon` / `daemon_status` functions, plus pidfile / status-file management; the `DaemonAlreadyRunning` exception. The machine-local **persistent project-root registry** also lives under `pid_dir` (the `PROJECT_ROOTS_FILENAME` constant → `DaemonConfig.project_roots_file`, e.g. `~/.se3/project_roots.json`), maintained by two helpers: `_read_project_roots(path)` (returns `[]` on missing / corrupt) and `_append_project_root(path, root)` (deduplicates by `realpath`, then atomically writes back via the existing `_atomic_write_json`); being placed under `pid_dir`, it automatically inherits the `SE3_DAEMON_DIR` / `DaemonConfig(pid_dir=...)` override and thereby naturally gains test isolation (tests isolate their writes with `DaemonConfig(pid_dir=tmp_path)` and do not pollute the real `~/.se3`). `Daemon.__init__` injects read / write callbacks based on `config.project_roots_file` (`registry_load` / `registry_persist`) into `DaemonAggregator` (using callbacks rather than a direct import to avoid a top-level aggregator↔daemon circular import), and changes the history reader's `project_roots_provider` from `aggregator.project_roots` (the bare active set) to `aggregator.all_project_roots`, so that `build_index` can still obtain the registry roots and correctly list on-disk history even with zero live processes or after a daemon restart
- `supervisor.py` — `DaemonSupervisor`, discovers and supervises the local `se3 run` processes (via `psutil` scanning and `engine.json` reading), tracking process lifecycle and cleanup. **Worktree attribution.** A `se3 run --worktree` flow body executes with its `cwd` inside `<main_root>/se3/worktrees/<name>/`, which is a transient isolation sandbox — NOT a project in its own right. When the supervisor discovers a process whose `cwd` lives under a `se3/worktrees/` directory, the module-level helper `resolve_worktree_main_root(path)` MUST map it back to the owning `<main_root>` (stripping exactly **one** `/se3/worktrees/<name>` suffix level, so a nested worktree resolves to its immediate parent, not the top), and the process MUST be attributed to `<main_root>` rather than registered as its own standalone project root; the companion predicate `is_worktree_copy_root(path)` identifies such worktree-copy roots so the aggregator can exclude them (see `aggregator.py`). This keeps the worktree sandbox out of the web console's project list and prevents the worktree copy from polluting the project-root registry
- `spawner.py` — `DaemonSpawner`, spawns new `se3 run --output-format json` subprocesses on others' behalf via `subprocess` (supporting remotely published new tasks), managing their arguments and environment; the `SpawnedProcess` record. It also exposes the `ensure_se3_project(project_root)` hook: it checks whether `<project_root>/se3/specs/base/spec.md` exists; if not, it runs `se3 init -p <project_root>` as a subprocess to complete initialization, and re-validates that the marker file exists after init returns; a failure at any stage is reported back to the caller via a structured `EnsureResult` / equivalent error (`client._handle_spawn` goes straight to the SPAWN_FAILED channel on ensure failure and does not proceed to spawn); when the directory is already an se3 project it is admitted directly, skipping init. Every time `client.py` handles `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` it must call this hook first, then delegate to the original spawn flow. The argv prefix when spawning an `se3` subprocess is resolved uniformly by the module-level helper `_resolve_se3_command()`, and all spawn paths (`spawn` / `spawn_init` / `spawn_run`) share its result; it is **strictly forbidden** to bypass it and call `shutil.which('se3')` directly or hardcode the `"se3"` literal — the bin directory of the daemon's own Python environment is not necessarily first on PATH (a typical scenario: the daemon runs in `~/.se3-stable` while a pixi/pip environment's bin directory comes earlier on PATH), and resolving by PATH would hit an older se3 console script in another environment, causing cross-version regressions such as the subprocess writing a `se3_version` into `_meta.json` that disagrees with the daemon, the discovery three-part user-content markers being absent, and `StreamJSONTracker` no longer writing `stream_progress` to the jsonl. `_resolve_se3_command()` uses a **same-prefix first** three-level fallback: (1) it prefers `Path(sys.executable).parent / 'se3'` (also probing `se3.exe` on Windows), returning `[<console_script>]` if it exists, guaranteeing the subprocess shares the same Python environment, wheel, and version as the daemon; (2) if the same-prefix one does not exist, it falls back to `[sys.executable, '-m', 'se3']`, reusing the same interpreter to load the `se3` package and avoiding PATH interference; (3) lastly it chooses `shutil.which('se3')` (effective only in extreme packaging scenarios such as a missing `sys.executable`). The return type stays `List[str]` (which may be a single-element `[path]` or `[python, '-m', 'se3']`), so the three call sites need no distinction when concatenating `argv`. To make configured agent commands resolvable when the daemon is started from an **impoverished launch environment** (systemd / cron / container), the spawner performs a one-time VSCode-style login-shell PATH resolution at construction time and merges its result into every spawned child's `PATH`: when the daemon is launched by systemd (`/etc/systemd/system/se3-daemon.service`, no `Environment=` line) it inherits systemd's minimal default `PATH` (`/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin`) which excludes `~/.local/bin`, so a flow spawned via `os.environ.copy()` inherits that bare `PATH`, and `claude_runner._run_single_with_monitor`'s `shutil.which(cmd)` then fails for every configured agent command (`dclaude` / `claude` / `kclaude`, etc., all installed under `~/.local/bin`) and the runner returns returncode 127, exhausting its polls and failing discovery — whereas `se3 run` from an interactive shell does not reproduce the failure because it inherits the shell's full `PATH`. Two module-level **pure** functions implement the fix (kept pure for unit testing): `resolve_login_shell_path(timeout)` runs `$SHELL -lc 'echo $PATH'` (falling back to `/bin/bash` when `$SHELL` is unset) under a short timeout to capture the login shell's full `PATH`, returning `None` on timeout / non-zero exit; and `merge_path_env(current, login)` returns the union as a `PATH` string with login-shell entries taking precedence (login entries first, the existing entries de-duplicated and appended after). `DaemonSpawner.__init__` resolves once and caches the result in `self._login_shell_path` (the spawner is constructed during daemon startup, so this satisfies "resolve once at startup and cache"); resolution failure **MUST NOT** block daemon startup — it falls back to the prior behaviour and logs a warning. Both spawn paths — `_launch()` and `ensure_se3_project()` — after building `child_env`, set `child_env['PATH']` to the merged result whenever the cache is non-empty, so any configured agent command resolves regardless of how impoverished the daemon's own launch environment is, aligning web-UI-initiated spawns with CLI behaviour. Under a full-`PATH` environment (terminal / CLI) the merge is idempotent (the login-shell entries are already present in the inherited `PATH`), so CLI behaviour is unchanged. This is a pure code-layer fix scoped by deliberate boundaries: it does NOT modify `/etc/systemd/system/se3-daemon.service`, does NOT add a config-layer PATH fallback, and does NOT pre-check agent commands at startup (agent configuration is project-level while the daemon is user-level, so at startup there may be no project yet). When a spawn request carries a non-empty `from_issue_id`, the spawner builds an `se3 run --from-issue <id> --output-format json` argv (appending `--discover` when the request's `discover` flag is set), reusing the same `_resolve_se3_command()` / merged-`PATH` machinery as the fresh-spawn path; the request's `task_description` is ignored because the issue's content becomes the task, and the issue lifecycle (pre-start in-progress transition, recording `source_issue_id` on the flow, and the post-run resolved/open write-back keyed on exit code) is fully delegated to the CLI's existing `--from-issue` handling rather than re-implemented in the daemon. The spawner also exposes a `resume(flow_id, project_root)` path that builds an `se3 run --resume --flow-id <id> --output-format json` argv (sharing the same `_resolve_se3_command()` / merged-`PATH` machinery as the fresh-spawn path) and is the daemon-side mechanism behind a server resume request: a `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` carrying `resume_flow_id` is routed by `client.py` to the daemon's resume handler (`Daemon._handle_resume_request` → `request_resume` → `spawner.resume`), which re-runs `se3 run --resume` against the project's existing on-disk `engine.json` so the persisted flow state supplies the task; the daemon best-effort guards against double-spawning a flow that already has a live `se3 run` process
- `aggregator.py` — `DaemonAggregator`, polls `se3/state/`, `se3/logs/`, `se3/calls/`, `se3/issues/` and aggregates them into a unified status snapshot (`MachineStatus`); `MachineStatus` also carries `project_roots: List[str]`, which the aggregator, on each snapshot round, merges from four sources via `all_project_roots()`, then deduplicates (normalizing by `realpath`) and stably sorts: (a) the roots actively registered by supervisor / spawner / client through the `_project_roots` set (containing only the active roots discovered / registered within the current process's lifetime, also the source for per-flow snapshot polling), (b) the machine-local **persistent project-root registry** (`DaemonConfig.pid_dir/project_roots.json`, see `daemon.py`) — any "project root that has run se3" is written through to disk via `add_project_root` on any registration path (spawn / ensure / resume / polling discovery, etc.), read back after a daemon restart, independent of live processes (write-through auto-registration: "run it and it's registered", with no pre-configuration needed), (c) all historical `project_root`s that `src/se3/daemon/history.py::enumerate_historical_project_roots()` adds from `se3/history/<flow_id>/_meta.json` and `se3/state/archive/engine_*.json` when it is fed the union "active roots ∪ registry roots", (d) any new root that was init-ed by `ensure_se3_project` before spawn (the client registers it back into `_project_roots` and likewise writes it through the registry via `add_project_root`). `add_project_root`, while adding to the in-memory active set, best-effort writes through to the persistent registry (deduplicated; the I/O is done via the injected `registry_load` / `registry_persist` callbacks), concentrating persistence at a single write-through point rather than scattering it across the four registration call sites, ensuring no registration is missed; `all_project_roots()` is the sole source of this merged view, both producing `MachineStatus.project_roots` via the `_merge_project_roots` delegate and serving as the `project_roots_provider` for the history index's `build_index` (see `daemon.py` / `history.py`), so that even with zero live processes, or after a daemon restart, neither the history list nor the New Task dropdown is empty anymore; per-flow snapshot polling (`get_snapshot`) still uses only the `_project_roots` active set, avoiding polling all historical roots every tick. To keep this merged view cheap on the hot path, `all_project_roots()` always merges the **active base** (`_project_roots ∪ registry_load`) immediately, but the expensive **disk historical enumeration** (`enumerate_historical_project_roots`, which walks the whole `se3/history` tree) is throttled behind a monotonic-clock TTL cache (`HISTORICAL_ROOTS_TTL`, currently `60s`) keyed/invalidated by a fingerprint of the active base, collapsing the per-tick full traversal to at most one walk per TTL window; the cache must be invalidated correctly without busting on the routine re-add of already-known active roots, and `add_project_root` proactively invalidates it so a newly registered root's history becomes visible promptly. This removes the per-status-tick full scan of `se3/history` that — when combined with the synchronous snapshot call on the event loop (see `client.py`) — stalled the daemon during task creation; only the discovery of purely historical roots is deferred by up to one TTL window, while new active / registered roots stay immediately visible. This field is reported via `STATUS_UPDATE` to drive the Project dropdown of the web New Task form, covering the "active set is empty but historical projects are still usable" scenario after a daemon restart; when enumerating pending-response calls under `se3/calls/`, items that already have a same-named response file (`.response` / `.response.json`) are skipped, to avoid a historically already-answered call being misreported as pending; besides this sibling-response determination, `_enumerate_calls` / `_snapshot_for_root` must also decide whether a pending call is still valid based on the flow's current progress: when a call's owning `context.step_id` is no longer the flow's current step (or that step has already been processed as `COMPLETED` / `REVISION`), the call must be removed from that flow's `pending_calls` even if no `.response` sibling file was written — because interactive calls answered at the CLI terminal (`call` / `cli_confirm` / `discovery_confirm`) are usually consumed directly by the run loop without writing a sibling file, otherwise a stale "awaiting reply" chip would never clear for the whole run; a call still sitting at the current unanswered step stays pending. In addition, for the same `(flow_id, step_id)` only the latest unanswered call is kept (`_dedup_calls_by_step`): discovery's multiple clarification rounds reuse the same `step_id`, writing a new call file each round, and once an old call is superseded by a new round it becomes a stale leftover and must be removed from that flow's `pending_calls` to prevent "awaiting reply" chips from accumulating; a call whose key cannot be located (missing `flow_id` or `step_id`) does not participate in deduplication and is kept as is. Each call file's `kind` field (`call` / `interjection` / `retry_decision` / `cli_confirm`, treated as `call` when absent) is parsed and, together with the `prompt` / `context` / `options` display metadata, enriched into a `PendingCall` and reported via `STATUS_UPDATE`, so the web console can render the various pending interactions differently by `kind`. In addition to calls, the aggregator reads each project's `se3/issues/` YAML files (via `_collect_issues`) into a list of `IssueSnapshot` entries carried on `MachineStatus.issues`, so the webui issue-management panel can list / filter / view issues without a second round-trip; each `IssueSnapshot` carries the webui-relevant fields (`id`, `project_root`, `description`, `status`, `tags`, `source`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, plus the optional `title` / `priority` / `type` which are omitted when unset), defaulting a missing `source` to `system` for legacy files, and unreadable issue files are skipped so a corrupt issue never breaks the snapshot. **Worktree issue de-duplication.** A `se3 run --worktree` flow clones the project's `se3/issues/` into its sandbox, so while the run is live both the main project root and the worktree-copy root would otherwise be aggregated and every issue would be counted twice. The aggregator MUST therefore skip issue collection for any project root that is a worktree copy (`is_worktree_copy_root`, see `supervisor.py`): during a worktree run only the main project's issues are authoritative, and the worktree copy's `se3/issues/` are ignored, so the webui issue list and counts are not doubled. (This is the same `se3/worktrees/` attribution that keeps the worktree directory out of the project list.) **Promoted worktree terminal state.** Because the merge-back promotes a completed worktree flow's terminal `engine.json` into the main project's `se3/state/archive/engine_<flow_id>.json` (see the `se3-workflows` spec), the aggregator/history layer reports that promoted snapshot as a `completed` flow exactly like an ordinary archived run, with no worktree special-case
- `client.py` — `DaemonClient`, maintains one outbound WebSocket connection to the central server (the daemon dials in actively, NAT-friendly), reporting aggregated status, receiving dispatched commands, and routing them to supervisor / spawner; the `websockets.connect` call is given `max_size=protocol.MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` so the daemon's inbound frame limit is lifted off the library's 1 MiB default to the shared protocol cap (set symmetrically for future large server→daemon frames, even though the daemon's send direction is unbounded by `max_size`); reconnects with exponential backoff after a disconnect; after connecting, reports the historical session index (`MSG_HISTORY_INDEX`), pushes active sessions' historical data in incremental append mode (`MSG_HISTORY_DATA`), handles inbound on-demand history pull requests (`MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST`) by replying with `MSG_HISTORY_DATA`, and handles inbound index re-push requests (`MSG_HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST`) — upon receipt it calls `_push_history(ws, force_index=True)` to force a rebuild and immediately re-push the latest history index (`force_index=True` bypasses the `engine.json`-change-based debounce so that a waiter suspended on `GET /api/history` at the server end receives the re-push promptly and thereby obtains the latest history rather than a stale last-pushed snapshot); because `build_index` is now TTL-cached in `history.py`, the `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST` handler first calls the reader's `invalidate_index_cache()` before the forced re-push, and likewise the push loop invalidates whenever `_history_changed()` fires (so a real `engine.json`/jsonl change rebuilds from disk instead of returning a within-TTL stale snapshot) and the `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` handler invalidates right after a successful spawn (so the freshly spawned flow's `engine.json` is included in both the index and the active-flow reads on the very next push instead of being delayed by the TTL window); all three call this method defensively via `getattr`, staying compatible with older reader stubs that lack it; to eliminate the runtime freeze of "the CLI has advanced but the web only sees it at the next status tick", the incremental history push is no longer driven solely by the fixed `status_interval` tick but by `engine.json` changes (detecting an `engine.json` mtime/content change triggers one mtime-debounced push), while the periodic tick is retained as a fallback; `_history_cursors` must advance correctly across ticks / across steps so that step progress of a running flow (including PAUSED/resume) is incrementally reflected to the web within one push cycle; when rebuilding the cursor table from this round's reads each round, for a **terminal flow that has no new records this round but is still an active flow in the current `engine.json`** (typically a flow waiting for `se3 run --resume` after FAILED), its existing cursor must be preserved — otherwise the flow would drop out of the cursor table after the last flush, and when `--resume` later flips the state back to RUNNING the missing cursor would force a full re-read and break the incremental push chain, freezing the web console on the failure snapshot; this preservation is bounded by the active `engine.json` flow set (one per root), so a terminal flow that has been fully read and already archived still drops out normally, keeping the cursor table bounded over the long run; handles inbound `MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW` by writing the mid-flight interjection typed in the web console as the target flow's `interjection`-kind call file, for that `se3 run` process to consume at the next step boundary. **The event loop must not be blocked by synchronous disk I/O**: synchronous calls that do heavy `Path.read_text` / directory traversal / JSON parsing — such as `HistoryReader.read_flow` in `_handle_history_request`, `build_index` in `_push_history` (including the forced rebuild / directory traversal when `force_index=True`), `read_active_flows` (fanning out to multiple per-step jsonl reads and `json.loads`), and the **`STATUS_UPDATE` snapshot construction** (the `self._snapshot_provider()` call in `_push_status`, and the same-source snapshot call in `_resolve_interject_root` and `_poll_once`) — must be executed in a worker thread via `asyncio.to_thread(...)`; the synchronous implementation stays in `daemon/history.py` / `daemon/aggregator.py`, and async only wraps a `to_thread` layer at the async entry points in daemon/client.py. The snapshot is offloaded because, through the aggregator's `all_project_roots` → `enumerate_historical_project_roots`, every status tick would otherwise walk the whole `se3/history` directory and read each `_meta.json` synchronously on the event loop; once history grows large this single synchronous traversal is enough to stall the loop, so the daemon misses heartbeats (the server's `HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` greys the machine out), drops inbound `SPAWN_FLOW` (no `SPAWN_FLOW handled`), and cannot even drive reconnection during the stall — manifesting as "creating a task in the web UI greys the machine out and it does not auto-recover until the daemon is manually restarted". This is so that when a session containing a large jsonl is selected, or a task is being created, the daemon can still keep responding to PING/PONG, PUSH, and new commands within the window of the server-side `HISTORY_PULL_TIMEOUT` and the client heartbeat timeout (`HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT`), avoiding the cascading regression of "504 while pulling history, the daemon judged offline at the same time, the machine greying out in the UI, and reconnect backoff triggered"; lightweight probe paths that only `stat` (such as signature scans like `active_flow_signature`) may stay synchronous and need no `to_thread`. When handling `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW`, the client first calls the daemon-internal ensure path (`_handle_ensure_request` → `spawner.ensure_se3_project`): if the target `project_root` is not an existing se3 project, it first runs `se3 init` as a subprocess on the daemon host, and on success registers the root into the aggregator's `_project_roots` before continuing the standard spawn flow; on ensure failure it notifies the server via the existing spawn-failure reporting channel (`SPAWN_FAILED` / equivalent error receipt) and does not enter the spawn phase. For the multi-tenant control plane, `DaemonClient` carries an optional `daemon_key` (empty for local / legacy single-tenant operation) and passes it into `make_hello` so the server can resolve `key → owner_id` and bind this machine to a trust domain; the key lives only in memory and on the HELLO wire and is never logged. On receiving the server's `WELCOME`, the client honours an `accepted=false` rejection (e.g. unknown/invalid daemon key): it records the server-supplied `reason` (which never contains the key), stops replaying the rejected key in a tight reconnect loop, and surfaces a message telling the operator to re-issue / fix the daemon key and restart, rather than hammering the server with a credential it has already rejected (the key is sourced once at daemon startup — see `DaemonConfig.daemon_key` below — and threaded through HELLO only). When handling `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW`, the client inspects the payload's optional `resume_flow_id`: when present it routes to the daemon's `resume_handler` (resuming the named flow via `spawner.resume` rather than a fresh spawn, skipping the `ensure_se3_project` init hook since a resumable flow's project already exists); when absent it follows the original ensure-then-spawn path. The client also handles `MSG_ISSUE_COMMAND` (`_handle_issue_command`): it validates the `project_root` (which must be an absolute, registered SE3-project path) by reusing the `project_roots` set cached from the most recent `STATUS_UPDATE` snapshot (`self._last_known_project_roots`, recorded by `_push_status` whenever it successfully builds a snapshot), falling back to building a single snapshot via `_snapshot_provider` **only** when that cache is still absent (e.g. an issue command arrives before the first `STATUS_UPDATE`); it MUST NOT re-invoke the heavyweight `_snapshot_provider` (which walks the whole `se3/history` tree) on every issue command, because that repeated heavy call on the issue hot path — racing the periodic status/history pushes that share the same ws connection — is what delayed the ack past the server's `ISSUE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` and produced the "issue already landed on disk but the web reported a timeout failure" false negative. After validation it executes the `create` / `edit` / `close` / `reopen` `operation` against `IssueManager` off the event loop (CLI/webui issue writes use `source="human"`). On a successful write it sends the `MSG_ISSUE_RESULT` ack (echoing `request_id`, reporting `ok` / `error` / affected `issue_id`, so the server can correlate the acknowledgment) **before** triggering the fast status push, not after: the ack is the frame the server blocks on within `ISSUE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`, and `_trigger_fast_push` (which only schedules a follow-up `STATUS_UPDATE`) must not be allowed to occupy the ws send order ahead of it — sending the ack first minimizes end-to-end ack latency while leaving the on-disk persistence semantics unchanged; the fast push still runs afterwards so the web reflects the issue change on the next tick
- `history.py` — historical session index construction and cursor-based incremental reading: enumerates `se3/history/` and `se3/state/archive/` to build the historical session index (task description, status, time, etc.), distinguishing active / inactive sessions; the `task_description` shown for a history-only flow (the list title) is recomputed live from the flow's first `*.jsonl` on every index build by `_extract_history_summary` — it is NOT persisted in `_meta.json`, so the title self-heals on existing flows with no data migration. That extractor follows a three-tier priority aligned with the web chat-history user bubble: (1) the user's literal input cut out by the shared `prompt_markers.extract_user_content` (the `USER_CONTENT` marker split, mirroring `splitUserPromptByMarker`); (2) failing that, the embedded `Task description:\s*-+\s*(.*?)\s*-+` block (the first-step-not-discovery `se3 run "task"` flow); (3) failing that, the raw first-line content untruncated (the index caller applies its own `_clip`). The CLI counterpart `PersistenceManager.extract_history_summary` (see the se3-commands spec) applies the identical three-tier priority, differing only in that it clips its own result to 100 characters. Reads incrementally by per-flow per-step jsonl file cursors, so an active session's conversation records can be reported incrementally without re-sending the whole jsonl each round. While reading, it also parses the authoritative step_type from each per-step jsonl filename (convention `NN_<step_type>_<hash>(_Gk)`) and injects it at the envelope layer, so each reported record looks like `{step_id, step_type, message}`: the raw `message` pushed by the daemon itself does not contain step_type, and after injection the frontend no longer has to guess from the filename, while the `message` content is left untouched to maintain backward compatibility and raw visibility. The parsing is done by the pure function `parse_step_type_from_step_id(stem)` — after stripping the leading `NN_` sequence number, the trailing `_G\d+` group suffix, and the trailing hexadecimal hash segment, it takes the remaining middle segment (which may itself contain underscores, e.g. `version_analyze`) as the step_type, softly validated against the built-in `_KNOWN_STEP_TYPES`; when the naming convention is followed but the type is unregistered it still returns the parsed middle segment (self-describing, drift-tolerant), while an old name with no sequence number and no hash (e.g. `commit_summary`) falls back to the original stem, never raising. The "active" determination of `read_active_flows` must cover **in-progress** flows (including `PAUSED` waiting for user input and the `--resume` continuation state), and must not prematurely drop a flow merely because it is not at the RUNNING terminal value, otherwise the web would freeze during a run and only catch up all at once after archiving; the incremental cursor must advance correctly on each round's read — newly appearing per-step jsonl files and appended lines of the same file must all be taken in, achieving **no loss, no duplication, no truncation of subsequent reads** (a record once read is never re-read, and an unread tail continues next round). To keep the daemon's per-fast-tick push loop (`client.py::_push_loop` → `_push_history`, which calls `build_index` every ~1s tick) from re-walking the whole `se3/history` tree every second — a second event-loop-starvation source distinct from, but of the same class as, the aggregator's `enumerate_historical_project_roots` walk already throttled by `HISTORICAL_ROOTS_TTL` — `build_index` caches its result behind a monotonic-clock TTL (`BUILD_INDEX_TTL`, currently `3s`): within the window it returns the cached `SessionMeta` list and only the uncached `_build_index_fresh()` performs the full directory walk + JSON parse, collapsing the repeated identical per-tick rebuilds into at most one walk per window. `invalidate_index_cache()` drops the cache so the next `build_index` rebuilds from disk; it is called on every real disk change (the push loop invalidates when `_history_changed()` fires), right after a flow is spawned, and before a forced index re-push (all three call sites live in `client.py`), so a newly spawned or just-changed flow becomes visible promptly rather than waiting out the TTL. Because the cached index may carry **stale `active` flags** for up to the TTL window, `read_active_flows` no longer trusts `meta.active` directly: it re-checks each candidate's live status via `_is_still_active`, a lightweight single-`engine.json` `stat` + small JSON parse (dramatically cheaper than the full rebuild it replaces) that confirms the on-disk `engine.json` still describes *this* `flow_id` (guarding against a different flow having since become the active `engine.json` flow, which would otherwise keep the stale meta in the active set and miss the new flow) and that its status is still an active one — so liveness is preserved (any real `engine.json` / jsonl change invalidates and rebuilds fresh, and the per-flow re-check catches within-window status flips) while the TTL collapses the redundant full walks that were starving the event loop. It also exports the helper `enumerate_historical_project_roots() -> list[str]`: it traverses `se3/history/<flow_id>/_meta.json` and `se3/state/archive/engine_*.json`, extracts each record's `project_root` field, and deduplicates and sorts them, for `aggregator.py` to merge into `MachineStatus.project_roots` when rebuilding the snapshot; when fed the union "active roots ∪ persistent registry roots" (rather than the active set only), it supplements each root in the union with its on-disk history roots, robustly skipping non-directory / artifact-less roots without raising. The two WARNING points that report an unreadable / corrupt archive or `_meta.json` file (`history: skipping unreadable meta file ...` and the sibling archive-file warning) are **per-file deduplicated** (`_warn_once_unreadable`): the first encounter of a given path logs at WARNING, and every subsequent encounter of the same path is demoted to DEBUG, so a small set of permanently corrupt meta files can no longer flood `daemon.log` (the observed failure produced a ~210MB / ~1.26M-line log from four corrupt `_meta.json` re-warned every tick). This dedup is a defence-in-depth backstop independent of, and complementary to, the TTL throttling of the enumeration in `aggregator.py` (which already drives the warning frequency down at the source); the corrupt files themselves are left in place and continue to be ignored. The `project_roots_provider` of the history index construction (`build_index`) is injected by the daemon as `aggregator.all_project_roots` (the ordered union of active roots ∪ registry roots ∪ the aforementioned on-disk history roots), replacing the previous approach of directly reading the bare active set `aggregator.project_roots` — the latter is empty when "this machine currently has no se3 run process", which was exactly the root cause of the history list previously always coming up empty (`No history sessions reported.`); after switching to `all_project_roots`, the history index is still non-empty with no live processes, or even after a daemon restart. To eliminate a second-order regression that 57b1609 (8.11.2)'s `BUILD_INDEX_TTL` cache addressed only partially — where the per-tick push loop still rebuilt the index roughly once per second (an active flow writing to disk every second fires `invalidate_index_cache()` via `client.py`, defeating the 3s TTL), and each `_build_index_fresh()` rebuild called `_extract_history_summary` on every history-only directory lacking a `_meta.json`, which read the entire first jsonl via `read_text()` just to take its first line (observed: 161 such directories, ~115MB of first jsonl including a single 30MB stale discovery log, sustaining ~100MB/s logical reads with a single core pinned at ~92% CPU by CPython's UTF-8 decode at ~104 MB/s; ZFS arcstats confirmed the reads were ~99.4% ARC-cache hits so the cost was single-core CPU burn and degraded daemon responsiveness rather than physical-array wear) — the whole-file reads in `history.py` are replaced by bounded reads via three changes:
  1. `_extract_history_summary` streams only the first line (`open()` + `readline()`) instead of `read_text()`, so recovering a title never reads the whole file; its three-tier output (the `prompt_markers.extract_user_content` user literal, then the `Task description:` block, then the raw first line) is unchanged, so the daemon→web title and its CLI counterpart (`PersistenceManager.extract_history_summary`, see the se3-commands spec) stay aligned.
  2. `DaemonHistoryReader` gains a process-internal per-directory meta cache (`self._history_meta_cache: Dict[str, Tuple[signature, SessionMeta]]`) keyed by a cheap directory content signature (the set of jsonl filenames + the latest mtime + total size, computed by reusing the existing `iterdir`/`stat` traversal); `_meta_from_history` returns the cached `SessionMeta` on a signature hit and only parses + back-fills on a miss, so a `_build_index_fresh` rebuild re-parses only the directories whose signature actually changed (an active flow's per-second write changes only its own directory's signature, while the other ~161 static directories all hit the cache). This is a process-internal optimization only: it does NOT write to disk and does NOT back-fill `_meta.json` into project directories (the daemon never writes into project directories on their behalf). It layers beneath the existing `BUILD_INDEX_TTL` cache: the TTL cache suppresses an entire rebuild on a no-change tick, while the per-directory signature cache suppresses re-parsing the unchanged directories during a rebuild that a real change did trigger.
  3. `read_flow` reads active flows incrementally by **byte offset** instead of `read_text().splitlines()` re-reading the whole jsonl every push and slicing by a line-number cursor. A process-internal `self._read_offsets: Dict[str, Tuple[consumed_lines, byte_offset, mtime, size]]` keyed by absolute jsonl path lets a push seek to the recorded offset and read only the appended bytes when the caller's line cursor matches the recorded consumed-line count and the file size is ≥ the recorded offset; otherwise (first read / cursor rewind / file truncated-and-replaced) it falls back to a from-scratch full read and rebuilds the offset, with the UTF-8 byte-boundary seek handled correctly. Only complete `\n`-terminated lines are consumed; a trailing partial line is left for the next round — a strictly safer compatibility improvement over the prior full-read path, which under a write race would treat a half-written line as bad JSON, skip it, and advance the cursor, dropping a record. The external `FlowRead` line-number cursor semantics and the pushed `records` content are preserved item-for-item, so server / webui keep using the `{jsonl-filename: line-count}` cursor unchanged; the offset table is reader-internal optimization state that never enters the wire protocol, so after a daemon restart it cold-starts and the first round degrades to a single full read, with correctness independent of it.
  The remaining file-read point `_read_json` was reviewed and left unchanged because it only reads small JSON files; these are the three file-read points in `history.py` (the first-jsonl title extractor, the active-flow incremental reader, and `_read_json`).

  **Worktree merge-back sidecar files.** When a `se3 run --worktree` flow merges back, each worktree per-step history file is written into the main session directory not as a plain `*.jsonl` but as a collision **sidecar** named `<base>.jsonl.from-<branch>` (e.g. `01_discovery_ab12.jsonl.from-worktree__b`), because the logical-step file may already exist in the main session. A reader that enumerates only `glob("*.jsonl")` never matches these sidecars, so every record after the first is dropped and the frontend renders empty content as "(no readable content)".
